# Feature: Chrome Launcher & BrowserProvider

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-003
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan.md`

Yantra's deterministic engine cannot do anything until a hardened Chrome session exists. This feature delivers that single entrypoint: a strategy-pattern `BrowserProvider` whose MVP implementation (`LocalBrowserProvider`) spawns the user's system Chrome over the CDP **pipe** transport (`--remote-debugging-pipe`, no WebSocket port), wires up per-workflow profile isolation (or ephemeral profile dirs for one-off sessions), and works identically on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

It also delivers `yantra doctor` v0 — the diagnostic surface a user runs when "it should work but doesn't": is Chrome installed and recent enough, is the data dir writable with owner-only perms, is the OS keychain reachable. Doctor never throws; it returns a structured `DoctorReport`.

Concretely this feature unblocks:
- FEAT-007 (`ask`) — needs ephemeral Chrome sessions.
- FEAT-008 (recorder) — needs visible Chrome with per-workflow profile.
- FEAT-010 (replay) — needs headless Chrome with per-workflow profile.
- FEAT-012 (CLI polish) — needs `yantra doctor` wired into the command surface.

**Why this matters as one feature:** the launcher, transport, profile manager, and doctor all share OS-portability concerns and the same set of paths/permissions. Splitting them would force duplicate OS-detection logic.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> Filesystem-only — no database in MVP. The "data model" here is on-disk artifacts plus the in-memory types that consume them. A `BrowserSession` table sketch is included as a forward-looking note for the Phase 2 daemon.

### On-Disk Artifacts

| Artifact | Path | Lifecycle | Permissions | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Per-workflow profile dir** | `~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/<workflow-name>/` | Persistent; created on first `record`/`run` of a workflow with `cookies: auto`. Survives across runs. | `0700` (Unix); ACL "owner-only" warned-on-violation (Windows). | `ProfileStore` |
| **Ephemeral profile dir** | `<os.tmpdir()>/yantra-<uuid>/` | Created at session start, deleted on `BrowserSession.close()` (best-effort on crash). Used by `ask`, `doctor`, and any workflow with `cookies: none`. | `0700` Unix; default ACL Windows. | `ProfileStore` |
| **Doctor cached report** | `~/.cache/yantra/doctor.json` | Written by `doctor()`; TTL 1 hour. Read-on-startup for fast checks; force-refresh via `yantra doctor --refresh`. | `0600`. | `doctor.ts` |
| **Yantra data root** | `~/.local/share/yantra/` (Unix), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\yantra\` (Windows) | Created on first use; doctor flags world-readable. | `0700` Unix. | shared paths helper |
| **Yantra cache root** | `~/.cache/yantra/` (Unix), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\yantra\Cache\` (Windows) | Created lazily by doctor. | `0700` Unix. | shared paths helper |

Path helpers honor `XDG_DATA_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME` on Linux when set.

### In-Memory Entities

```ts
// packages/core/src/browser/types.ts (shared)

/** Discovered Chrome installation. */
interface ChromeInstall {
  readonly path: string;          // absolute path to chrome / chrome.exe / google-chrome
  readonly version: string;       // SemVer-ish string parsed from `--version`
  readonly majorVersion: number;  // parsed; used by doctor for min-version check
  readonly channel: "stable" | "beta" | "dev" | "canary" | "chromium" | "unknown";
  readonly source: "system";      // future: "bundled" (Phase 2)
}

/** Options passed to BrowserProvider.launch. Zod-validated. */
interface LaunchOptions {
  readonly profile: ProfileSpec;
  readonly headless: boolean;     // false for record/doctor; true otherwise
  readonly viewport: { width: number; height: number } | null;
  readonly extraArgs: readonly string[];     // appended after Yantra's hardened args
  readonly env: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  readonly startupTimeoutMs: number;          // default 15_000
  readonly chromeOverridePath: string | null; // for tests / power users
}

/** How profile dir is resolved. Discriminated union. */
type ProfileSpec =
  | { kind: "workflow"; workflowName: string } // ~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/<name>/
  | { kind: "ephemeral" }                      // <tmp>/yantra-<uuid>/
  | { kind: "explicit"; absolutePath: string };// power-user escape hatch; doctor validates

/** Strategy interface. MVP impl: LocalBrowserProvider. Phase 3+: RemoteBrowserProvider. */
interface BrowserProvider {
  launch(options: LaunchOptions): Promise<BrowserSession>;
  detectChrome(): Promise<ChromeInstall | null>;
}

/** Live browser handle returned from launch. Wraps puppeteer-core but does NOT leak it. */
interface BrowserSession {
  readonly id: string;             // UUID for log correlation
  readonly chrome: ChromeInstall;
  readonly profilePath: string;
  newPage(): Promise<Page>;        // see locator engine feature (FEAT-004) for Page interface
  close(): Promise<void>;          // idempotent; cleans ephemeral profile if applicable
  on(event: BrowserSessionEvent, handler: (...args: unknown[]) => void): void;
}

type BrowserSessionEvent =
  | "crashed"      // pipe closed unexpectedly → BrowserCrashedError context
  | "disconnected" // graceful disconnect
  | "page-created" // new target attached
  | "page-closed"; // target detached

/** Result of `yantra doctor`. Doctor NEVER throws — always returns this. */
interface DoctorReport {
  readonly generatedAt: string;             // ISO-8601
  readonly cachedFrom: string | null;       // ISO-8601 if served from cache; null if fresh
  readonly overall: "ok" | "warn" | "error";
  readonly checks: readonly DoctorCheck[];
}

interface DoctorCheck {
  readonly id:
    | "chrome.detected"
    | "chrome.version_min"
    | "datadir.writable"
    | "datadir.permissions"
    | "cachedir.writable"
    | "keychain.reachable";
  readonly status: "ok" | "warn" | "error";
  readonly message: string;
  readonly details: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; // structured context for --json
  readonly fixHint: string | null;                     // e.g., "Install Chrome from https://..."
}
```

### Repository-Style Interfaces

```ts
/** Abstraction over profile-dir lifecycle. Implementation in profile-store.ts. */
interface ProfileStore {
  /** Resolve a ProfileSpec to a concrete, writable, 0700-perms directory. */
  resolve(spec: ProfileSpec): Promise<ResolvedProfile>;

  /** List persistent (workflow) profile dirs that currently exist on disk. */
  listWorkflowProfiles(): Promise<readonly WorkflowProfileEntry[]>;

  /** Remove a workflow's persistent profile dir (used by future `yantra forget <wf>`). */
  removeWorkflowProfile(workflowName: string): Promise<void>;

  /** Best-effort cleanup of an ephemeral dir. Idempotent; never throws. */
  cleanupEphemeral(absolutePath: string): Promise<void>;
}

interface ResolvedProfile {
  readonly absolutePath: string;
  readonly kind: ProfileSpec["kind"];
  readonly createdNow: boolean;        // true on first resolve
}

interface WorkflowProfileEntry {
  readonly workflowName: string;
  readonly absolutePath: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly lastModified: string;       // ISO-8601
}
```

The `BrowserProvider` strategy slot is what swaps for the Phase 3+ `RemoteBrowserProvider` (CDP over WSS to a worker host). MVP only ships `LocalBrowserProvider`.

### Forward-Looking DB Schema Sketch (Phase 2 daemon — not built here)

When the Phase 2 daemon arrives, profile metadata moves to SQLite. Capturing the sketch now so the on-disk format stays compatible:

```sql
-- Phase 2 only. NOT created by this feature. Documented for forward-compat.
CREATE TABLE browser_profile (
  workflow_name     TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,
  absolute_path     TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  chrome_path_used  TEXT    NOT NULL,        -- ChromeInstall.path at last use
  chrome_version    TEXT    NOT NULL,        -- ChromeInstall.version at last use
  created_at        TEXT    NOT NULL,
  last_used_at      TEXT    NOT NULL,
  size_bytes        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE INDEX idx_browser_profile_last_used ON browser_profile (last_used_at);
```

### Relationships

- One `BrowserProvider` produces 1:N `BrowserSession` instances over its lifetime.
- Each `BrowserSession` is bound to exactly one `ResolvedProfile`.
- Each `ResolvedProfile.kind = "workflow"` maps 1:1 to a Workflow (owned by FEAT-009/010).
- Each `ResolvedProfile.kind = "ephemeral"` lives and dies inside one session.

### Indexes & Constraints (filesystem-level)

- **Unique constraint**: workflow profile names must be unique on disk (enforced by filesystem; collision detection on `resolve` returns the existing dir).
- **Permission constraint**: any path under `~/.local/share/yantra/` is created with mode `0700`. Doctor flags violations as `warn`.
- **Forbidden constraint**: the profile dir resolver MUST refuse paths inside the user's real Chrome profile (e.g., `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data`, `~/.config/google-chrome`). Throws `ProfilePathRefusedError`.

Re-exports inferred type via `z.infer`.

- `packages/core/src/browser/launcher.ts` — `launchChrome(opts, chrome)` internal: spawns `chrome` with hardened arg list + `--remote-debugging-pipe`, wires CDP transport over child stdio fds 3/4 (null-delimited JSON), connects puppeteer-core, returns the live `Browser` puppeteer handle. Handles per-OS spawn quirks (Windows `detached:false` and CTRL+BREAK signaling; macOS/Linux `SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL`).
- `packages/core/src/browser/session.ts` — `LocalBrowserSession implements BrowserSession`. Wraps puppeteer `Browser`; exposes `newPage()` returning a thin `Page` facade (just enough surface — `goto`, `evaluate`, `close`, `on('framenavigated')` — so the locator engine in FEAT-004 can layer on top); event plumbing for `crashed`/`disconnected`. Owns ephemeral-profile cleanup on `close()`.
- `packages/core/src/browser/provider.ts` — `LocalBrowserProvider implements BrowserProvider`. Constructor takes `{ profileStore, logger, clock }` for DI. `launch()` orchestrates: validate `LaunchOptions` (Zod) → resolve profile → discover Chrome (with override path) → launch → wrap in session.
- `packages/core/src/browser/doctor.ts` — `doctor(opts?: { refresh?: boolean }): Promise<DoctorReport>` (never throws). Runs the 6 checks below; reads/writes `~/.cache/yantra/doctor.json` with 1-hour TTL; respects `--refresh` flag (passed in by the future CLI in FEAT-012).
- `packages/core/src/browser/paths.ts` — OS-aware path helpers: `dataDir()`, `cacheDir()`, `profilesRoot()`, `ephemeralRoot()`, `doctorCachePath()`. Honors `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `LOCALAPPDATA`.

## 4. Dependencies

**Internal (other Yantra features):**

- **FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI)** — required. Provides `packages/core/`, TS strict config, Vitest, fast-check, cross-OS CI matrix. The integration test in TASK-008 specifically rides the CI matrix.
- **FEAT-002 (Yantra Protocol v0)** — required for type-only imports of `TaskEvent` shape (forward reference; this feature does not emit events directly but its `BrowserCrashedError` is consumed by the executor in FEAT-005 to produce a `task_failed` event).
- **No dependency on FEAT-006** (Security Envelope) — keychain reachability check in doctor uses `keytar` directly with a synthetic key/value (`yantra.doctor.probe`). FEAT-006 will later wrap keytar behind `KeychainProvider`; this feature exposes a small internal helper that the FEAT-006 abstraction can absorb without API churn.

**External (npm):**

- `puppeteer-core` (latest stable, pinned major) — CDP transport + target attach. We use only `Browser`, `Page`, `connect()`, `launch()` (with `pipe: true`) for the wrapping.
- `zod` (already in workspace) — `LaunchOptions` schema.
- `keytar` (already in workspace per memory.md) — doctor's keychain check only; full secrets API lives in FEAT-006.
- `fast-check` (dev) — property tests.
- `vitest` (dev) — unit + integration runner.

**External tools (NOT bundled):**

- The user's system **Chrome** (or Chromium / Chrome derivatives — Edge/Brave detected but warned-not-supported in MVP). Bundled Chromium is Phase 2.

**Notes:**

- No `which` npm package — we inline a 20-line `whichSync` helper (Linux/macOS) that walks `PATH`. On Windows, we use registry reads + standard-paths fallback. The `which` package is small but the inline version is smaller and dependency-free.
- No dependency on Node's experimental `child_process` features. `spawn` with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']` is stable since Node 18.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

> Vertical slices. Each slice produces something testable end-to-end at its level (discovery resolves a path, launcher boots Chrome, doctor returns a report). Tasks are ordered so a coding agent can start at TASK-001 and have something runnable by TASK-003. Tasks 004–006 layer on profile management, session lifecycle, and resource hygiene. Tasks 007–010 round out doctor, integration, crash handling, and security hardening.

### TASK-001: Cross-OS Chrome discovery

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `chrome-discovery.ts`. Export `detectChrome(opts?: { override?: string }): Promise<ChromeInstall | null>` plus internal helpers. Platform branches:
  - **macOS**: probe in order: `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome`, `/Applications/Google Chrome Beta.app/...`, `/Applications/Google Chrome Canary.app/...`, `~/Applications/Google Chrome.app/...`, then `$PATH` lookup of `google-chrome` and `chromium`. Run `--version` to confirm and parse channel.
  - **Windows**: read registry first — `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\chrome.exe` (default value) and `HKCU\...\App Paths\chrome.exe`. Fallback paths: `%ProgramFiles%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`, `%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`. Use `reg query` via `child_process.execFileSync` (do not depend on `winreg` package; spawn is sufficient and avoids a native binding).
  - **Linux**: `$PATH` walk for `google-chrome`, `google-chrome-stable`, `chromium`, `chromium-browser`, then standard paths `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, `/usr/local/bin/google-chrome`, `/snap/bin/chromium`, `/opt/google/chrome/chrome`.
  - **Version parsing**: shell out `<path> --version`, parse `Google Chrome 124.0.6367.91` → `{version:"124.0.6367.91", majorVersion:124}`. Channel inferred from path/name.
  - **Override path**: if `opts.override` provided, validate it exists + executable + `--version` works; bypass discovery.
  - Returns `null` if nothing found. **Never throws** for "not found" — that is signalled via `null` so doctor can render it cleanly.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: With mocked `fs.access`, `fs.stat`, `child_process.execFileSync`, `child_process.spawnSync` per OS:
  - macOS: finds Chrome in `/Applications`; finds Canary when stable missing; returns null when nothing exists.
  - Windows: prefers HKLM over HKCU; falls back to Program Files when registry empty; handles missing `reg` binary (rare CI image) gracefully.
  - Linux: returns first hit on PATH; honors snap path; returns null when none.
  - Version parser: handles `Google Chrome 124.0.6367.91`, `Chromium 122.0.6261.94`, malformed output (returns `version:"unknown"`, `majorVersion:0`).
  - Override path: rejects non-existent path; rejects unexecutable; accepts valid.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `detectChrome`, `ChromeInstall`, and platform-branch helpers. Inline note pointing to the brainstorm §5 (cross-platform paths gotcha). README of `packages/core/` documents that `BrowserProvider` is the only sanctioned way to launch Chrome.
- **Verify**: Unit tests pass on all 3 OS images in CI. Manual sanity: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core exec node -e "import('./dist/browser/chrome-discovery.js').then(m=>m.detectChrome()).then(console.log)"` prints a `ChromeInstall` on each developer's machine.

### TASK-003: `LocalBrowserProvider.launch()` over CDP pipe

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Create `launcher.ts` with internal `launchChrome(opts: LaunchOptions, chrome: ChromeInstall, profile: ResolvedProfile): Promise<{ browser: PuppeteerBrowser; child: ChildProcess }>`.
    - Build arg list: `HARDENED_BASE_ARGS` + `--user-data-dir=<profile.absolutePath>` + `--remote-debugging-pipe` + (if `opts.headless`) `--headless=new` + (if `opts.viewport`) `--window-size=W,H` + `opts.extraArgs`.
    - **Never** include `--remote-debugging-port`. Pipe transport only.
    - `spawn(chrome.path, args, { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'], env: { ...process.env, ...opts.env }, detached: false, windowsHide: true })`.
    - Connect puppeteer-core via `puppeteer.connect({ transport: pipeTransport(child) })` where `pipeTransport` wraps child fd 3 (write) and fd 4 (read) into the null-delimited JSON framing puppeteer expects. (Implementation cribbed from Playwright's pipe transport — Apache-2.0; include attribution comment.)
    - Apply a 15s deadline via `Promise.race`; on timeout: capture last 4KB of stderr, kill the child, throw `BrowserLaunchError` with that context.
    - On clean connect: return `{ browser, child }`.
  - Create `provider.ts` exporting `LocalBrowserProvider implements BrowserProvider`:
    - Constructor: `{ profileStore: ProfileStore; clock?: () => Date; logger?: Logger }`.
    - `detectChrome()` delegates to `chrome-discovery.detectChrome({ override: undefined })`.
    - `launch(opts)`:
      1. `parseLaunchOptions(opts)` → typed options.
      2. `profileStore.resolve(opts.profile)` → `ResolvedProfile`.
      3. `detectChrome({ override: opts.chromeOverridePath ?? undefined })`; if `null` throw `ChromeNotFoundError`; if `majorVersion < MIN_SUPPORTED_CHROME_MAJOR` throw `ChromeVersionUnsupportedError`.
      4. Log `info` `"launching Chrome <majorVersion> from <path>"` — **never log the args list** (profile path may be PII-bearing); under `--debug` log args only with the profile path redacted to `<profile>`.
      5. `launchChrome(opts, chrome, profile)` → `{ browser, child }`.
      6. Wrap into `LocalBrowserSession` (TASK-005) and return.

  - `--remote-debugging-port` never appears.
  - `--user-data-dir` always points to resolved profile.
  - Startup timeout: spawn never connects → throws `BrowserLaunchError` with stderr captured.
  - Override path: short-circuits discovery.
  - Chrome version 119 → `ChromeVersionUnsupportedError`.
  - Chrome not found → `ChromeNotFoundError`.
  - Logger: does not log full args at `info` level; redacts profile path under `debug`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `LocalBrowserProvider`, `BrowserProvider` interface, `launchChrome`. README adds "Launching a browser" code sample.

### TASK-004: `LocalProfileStore` with refused-path guard and perms

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `profile-store.ts`: `LocalProfileStore implements ProfileStore`.
  - `resolve(spec)`:
    - `workflow`: target = `paths.profilesRoot() + '/' + workflowName`. Validate `workflowName` against `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/`; reject otherwise with a clear error (no `Error` swallow — typed `ProfilePathRefusedError`). Run `assertNotInsideRealChromeProfile(target)` (refused-path guard).  `mkdir -p` with mode `0700` on Unix; on Windows `mkdir` then best-effort ACL trim (out of scope to fully solve on Windows — just create + warn via doctor). Return `{absolutePath, kind, createdNow}`.
    - `ephemeral`: target = `paths.ephemeralRoot() + '/yantra-' + randomUUID()`. `mkdir` with mode `0700`. Return.
    - `explicit`: target = the provided absolute path. Validate exists, is a directory, is writable, mode is `0700` on Unix (warn-not-error on Windows). Run refused-path guard. Return with `createdNow:false`.
  - `assertNotInsideRealChromeProfile(p)`: refuses if `p` is at or below any of: `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome`, `~/Library/Application Support/Chromium`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Chromium\User Data`, `~/.config/google-chrome`, `~/.config/chromium`. Throws `ProfilePathRefusedError`.
  - `listWorkflowProfiles()`: `readdir` of `paths.profilesRoot()`; for each, `stat` for size + mtime.
  - `removeWorkflowProfile(name)`: validate name → `rm -rf` recursively; idempotent.
  - `cleanupEphemeral(absPath)`: idempotent, catches and logs `warn` on EBUSY (Chrome process may still hold a lock on Windows shortly after exit).

  - `cleanupEphemeral` idempotent; survives non-existent path; survives EBUSY (mocked).
  - `listWorkflowProfiles` sorted by lastModified desc.

### TASK-005: `LocalBrowserSession` + `Page` facade

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `session.ts`: `LocalBrowserSession implements BrowserSession`.
  - Constructor takes `{ browser: PuppeteerBrowser; child: ChildProcess; chrome: ChromeInstall; profile: ResolvedProfile; profileStore: ProfileStore; logger: Logger }`.
  - `id = randomUUID()`.
  - `newPage()`: `await browser.newPage()`; wrap in a minimal `Page` facade type defined in `types.ts` exposing `goto(url, opts?)`, `evaluate(fn, ...args)`, `close()`, `url()`, `on('framenavigated', handler)`. This is intentionally the smallest surface FEAT-004 (locator engine) needs; we extend in that feature, not here. Emit `page-created`.
  - `on(event, handler)`: simple emitter; map puppeteer's `browser.on('disconnected')` to our `disconnected` AND `crashed` (decision made in TASK-009 based on child exit code at disconnect time).
  - `close()`: idempotent. Sequence: `await browser.close()` with 5s timeout → if still alive, `child.kill('SIGTERM')` (Unix) / `child.kill()` then `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F` on Windows after 2s grace → `await profileStore.cleanupEphemeral(profile.absolutePath)` **only if** `profile.kind === 'ephemeral'`. Log `info` `"browser session <id> closed"`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (puppeteer fully mocked):
  - `newPage` emits `page-created`.
  - `close()` is idempotent — second call is a no-op.
  - `close()` cleans ephemeral profile dir, leaves persistent workflow profile intact.
  - `close()` honors the 5s puppeteer-close timeout then falls back to `child.kill`.
  - `on('crashed')` fires when child exits non-zero before `close()` invoked.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `BrowserSession`, `Page` facade type, and lifecycle. README's "Launching a browser" sample extended with `session.newPage()`.
- **Verify**: Tests green.

### TASK-007: `yantra doctor` v0 diagnostics

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `doctor.ts` exports `doctor(opts?: { refresh?: boolean }): Promise<DoctorReport>`. **Never throws.** Every check is wrapped in `try { ... } catch (e) { return errorCheck(id, e) }`.
  - Cache: if `!opts.refresh` and `~/.cache/yantra/doctor.json` is fresh (`generatedAt + 1h > now`), return it with `cachedFrom = generatedAt`. Otherwise run all checks fresh, write cache, return with `cachedFrom: null`. Cache file written with mode `0600`.
  - Checks (each returns a `DoctorCheck`):
    1. **`chrome.detected`**: `detectChrome()`. `ok` if found, `error` if `null` with `fixHint:"Install Chrome from https://www.google.com/chrome/"`.
    2. **`chrome.version_min`**: `ok` if `majorVersion >= MIN_SUPPORTED_CHROME_MAJOR`; else `error` with hint to update; `skipped` (status:`warn`, message:"chrome not detected") if previous check was `error`.
    3. **`datadir.writable`**: `fs.access` on `paths.dataDir()` with `W_OK`; create if missing; `ok` / `error`.
    4. **`datadir.permissions`**: on Unix, `stat` `paths.dataDir()`; `warn` if mode includes group/other read/write/exec (`mode & 0o077 !== 0`). On Windows, always `ok` with a `details.note: "owner-only ACL not enforced on Windows in v0"`.
    5. **`cachedir.writable`**: same as 3 for `paths.cacheDir()`.
    6. **`keychain.reachable`**: `keytar.setPassword('yantra-doctor', 'probe', 'ok')` → `keytar.getPassword(...)` → `keytar.deletePassword(...)`. `ok` round-trip; `error` with `e.message` in `details` otherwise. (Hint: "macOS: unlock keychain. Linux: install libsecret + a keyring like gnome-keyring. Windows: should work out of the box.")
  - `overall` rollup: `error` if any check is `error`; `warn` if any is `warn` and none `error`; else `ok`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (all mocked — no real Chrome / keychain):
  - Each check fails in isolation → `overall` reflects severity.
  - All checks pass → `overall = ok`.
  - Cache hit returns cached report with `cachedFrom` set; cache stale forces re-run.
  - `refresh:true` bypasses cache.
  - Doctor with **every** check throwing internally still returns a `DoctorReport` (the never-throws property — assert as `fast-check` property).
  - Permission check `warn`s on `0o755`, `ok`s on `0o700`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `doctor`, `DoctorReport`, `DoctorCheck`. README adds "Running `yantra doctor`" with sample JSON output.
- **Verify**: Tests green. Manual: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core exec node -e "import('./dist/browser/doctor.js').then(m=>m.doctor()).then(r=>console.log(JSON.stringify(r,null,2)))"` prints a `DoctorReport` whose `overall` is `ok` on a healthy dev machine.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001, TASK-002, TASK-004.

### TASK-009: Connection-loss handling — Chrome crashes mid-session

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - In `session.ts`, install a listener on the puppeteer `browser.on('disconnected')` and on the child process `child.on('exit', (code, signal) => ...)`.
  - **Classification rule** — `crashed` vs `disconnected`:
    - If `close()` was called → emit `disconnected` only, never `crashed`.
    - If `child.exitCode !== 0` and we did not call `close()` → emit `crashed` with a context object `{ exitCode, signal, lastStderr }` (last 4KB of buffered stderr).
    - If `child.exitCode === 0` and we did not call `close()` → still emit `crashed` (the user did not ask for shutdown; this is unexpected) but with `exitCode: 0` so the executor can downgrade severity if it wants.
  - Construct a `BrowserCrashedError` carrying `{sessionId, exitCode, signal, lastStderr}` and pass it to `crashed` handlers as the first argument.
  - **Cleanup on crash**: even though `close()` was not called, `cleanupEphemeral` runs in the `child.on('exit')` handler (best-effort, swallow errors and log `warn`) so we don't leak temp dirs on crash.
  - Mark the session "dead" — subsequent `newPage()` rejects with `BrowserCrashedError`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Simulate `child.emit('exit', 139, null)` (SIGSEGV) → `crashed` listener invoked with `exitCode:139`.
  - After crash, `newPage()` rejects with `BrowserCrashedError`.
  - After crash on ephemeral session, ephemeral dir is cleaned.
  - `close()` called BEFORE `child.exit` → only `disconnected` emitted, never `crashed`.
  - `close()` is still idempotent after a crash.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `BrowserCrashedError`, the `crashed` event, and the cleanup semantics. README adds a "Handling crashes" subsection.
- **Verify**: Tests green. The executor in FEAT-005 will subscribe to `crashed` and emit a `task_failed` event — this feature's responsibility ends at "emit a structured event with usable context."
- **Depends on**: TASK-005.

### TASK-010: Security hardening — profile-dir permissions + doctor surfacing

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - In `profile-store.ts`'s `resolve` for kind `workflow` and `explicit`: after `mkdir`, on Unix `chmod(absolutePath, 0o700)`; verify with `stat` and throw `ProfilePathRefusedError` with hint if the mode is anything else (e.g., user has a restrictive umask that yielded a stricter mode — accept that; but reject looser modes like `0o755`).
  - On Windows: skip chmod; instead, on first creation, attempt to remove inherited ACLs for `Users` group via `icacls "<path>" /inheritance:r /grant:r "%USERNAME%:(OI)(CI)F"`. If `icacls` fails (rare on home editions), log a `warn` — do not throw. Doctor reports this as a `warn`-level finding for the user.
  - Doctor check 4 (`datadir.permissions`) already from TASK-007 — extend to also walk `paths.profilesRoot()` and flag any per-workflow profile dir whose mode is not `0700` on Unix. Returns `warn` with a `details.offenders: string[]` list.
  - In `launcher.ts`: when emitting the `info`-level "launching Chrome" log, the full args list is **never** included at `info`; under `debug`, the profile path is redacted to `<profile>` and replaced with the workflow name when known (`ResolvedProfile.kind === 'workflow'` ? workflowName : `<ephemeral>`).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - On Unix: a profile dir created with `umask 022` has its mode corrected to `0o700` after resolve.
  - On Unix: manually `chmod 0o755` a workflow profile then run doctor — `datadir.permissions` returns `warn` listing that profile in `details.offenders`.
  - On Windows (or with platform mocked): doctor's permission check returns `ok` with the documented note.
  - Logger does not log the profile path at `info`; under `debug`, profile path is redacted/replaced.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: README "Security notes" subsection: "Yantra creates per-workflow profile dirs with `0700` permissions on Unix. On Windows v0 we attempt to trim inherited ACLs; this is best-effort and `yantra doctor` will warn if your data dir is world-readable. Yantra never logs the full Chrome command line because it contains the profile path."
- **Verify**: Tests green. Manual on Unix: `ls -ld ~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/*` shows `drwx------`. Manual: `yantra doctor` (once FEAT-012 wires it) returns `warn` after `chmod 0755` on a profile.
- **Depends on**: TASK-004, TASK-007.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. This feature does not authenticate. The doctor's `keychain.reachable` check uses keytar with a synthetic key (`yantra-doctor / probe`) and deletes the value before returning — it never touches real user secrets. FEAT-006 will eventually wrap keytar behind `KeychainProvider`; the doctor's direct keytar import is the only place in `core` allowed to bypass that wrapper (carry a `// eslint-disable-next-line yantra/keychain-via-provider — doctor must work before FEAT-006 lands` comment).

- **Error Handling**: Per memory.md, every domain failure has a typed custom error class extending `Error`. This feature introduces:
  - `ChromeNotFoundError` — discovery returned `null` and no override given. Carries the OS name and the paths probed.
  - `ChromeVersionUnsupportedError` — Chrome found but `majorVersion < MIN_SUPPORTED_CHROME_MAJOR`. Carries `{found, required}`.
  - `BrowserLaunchError` — anything between `spawn` and successful CDP handshake. Carries `{phase, lastStderr, args (redacted)}`.
  - `BrowserCrashedError` — child exited unexpectedly. Carries `{sessionId, exitCode, signal, lastStderr}`.
  - `ProfilePathRefusedError` — refused-path guard fired, or profile permissions are unsafe. Carries `{path, reason}`.
  - `KeychainUnreachableError` — only constructed by doctor's keychain check; not thrown (wrapped into a `DoctorCheck` entry).
  - **`doctor()` returns `Result<DoctorReport, never>`** — it absolutely never throws. Every internal check is wrapped; uncaught errors are converted to `DoctorCheck { status: "error", message: <stringified error>, details: { stack } }`. This is asserted by a property test.

- **Logging**: Pino, per memory.md. Levels:
  - `info` — `"launching Chrome <major>.<x>.<y> from <path>"`; `"browser session <id> closed"`.
  - `warn` — Windows ACL trim failed; profile dir permission anomaly; ephemeral cleanup EBUSY.
  - `error` — launch failure with `BrowserLaunchError`; doctor cache write failure (degrades gracefully — no cache, still returns report).
  - `debug` — full args list **with profile path redacted**; CDP messages framing summary (just `{direction, method, payloadSize}` — no payload contents); discovery probe attempts.
  - **Never log**: the raw profile path (it can encode the workflow name which may be sensitive); the resolved override path (user power-flag); the args list at any level above debug.

- **Security**:
  - **CDP-pipe only** — `--remote-debugging-pipe`. The launcher rejects `--remote-debugging-port` in `extraArgs`. This eliminates the localhost-port attack surface from puppeteer-core's default transport (per plan §6).
  - **Profile permissions `0700`** on Unix; warn-not-block on Windows (TASK-010).
  - **Refused-path guard** — the resolver refuses to write to the user's real Chrome profile dirs (per brainstorm §5: "Never read from `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome` or `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/User Data` directly").
  - **No literal profile paths in logs** at `info` or above.
  - **Doctor cache file** mode `0600`.
  - **Keychain probe** key is `yantra-doctor / probe`, value is the literal string `"ok"`, deleted before returning. Carries no user data.

- **Testing**:
  - All unit tests tagged `@no-llm` (per memory.md, this feature is on the spine — mandatorily LLM-free).
  - Integration test (TASK-008) tagged `@no-llm` and gated on `YANTRA_E2E_BROWSER=1`. CI installs Chrome on each OS runner.
  - Property test (TASK-006) on the launch/close cycle — non-optional per memory.md's "Property-based tests are non-optional for..." Strictly, the listed required surfaces are sanitizer, protocol validator, and scope enforcer; the launcher's leak-freedom is treated with equal rigor here because resource leaks compound catastrophically over a long-lived user session.
  - Cross-OS matrix: every spec runs on `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest` from day one (per memory.md). The chrome-discovery tests are explicitly OS-aware.

## Notes for the Implementer (non-normative)

- The pipe transport implementation is the trickiest piece — Playwright's `src/server/chromium/pipeTransport.ts` is the reference. Apache-2.0 licensed; lift with attribution. Null-delimited JSON framing, one message per `\0`-terminated chunk.
- `puppeteer-core`'s `launch({ pipe: true })` does this internally; verify whether the puppeteer-core version pinned by FEAT-001 already exposes the pipe transport without us re-implementing it. If yes, TASK-003's "wrap fd 3/4" work shrinks to "pass `pipe:true` and inherit". If no (older puppeteer-core), implement the framing ourselves.
- `MIN_SUPPORTED_CHROME_MAJOR = 120` is a placeholder — pin it to whatever the pinned `puppeteer-core` major declares as its minimum at implementation time. Revisit on every puppeteer-core bump.
- Edge / Brave / Vivaldi all expose CDP via the same flags but are out of scope for v0. Discovery may surface them in logs but `provider.launch` only accepts a `ChromeInstall` whose `channel ∈ {stable, beta, dev, canary, chromium}`. TODO entry for "support Edge/Brave as first-class" goes in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`.
